code:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "mylang-cs374"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A small programming language built in CS374"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = {text = "MIT"}

[project.scripts]
mylang = "mylang.__main__:main"
description: The single file that describes your Python package to PyPI, to pip, and to the build tool: build system, project metadata, and the console-script entry point.

steps.description: This is `pyproject.toml`, the single file that describes your package to PyPI, to `pip`, and to the build tool. The page says to create it in the root of your project, next to the `mylang/` directory. `[build-system]` names the tools that build the package: `setuptools` and `wheel`, with `setuptools.build_meta` as the backend.

`[project]` holds the package metadata. `name` must be unique on PyPI, and the page says to append your username or course section if `mylang-cs374` is taken. `version` must be bumped every time you upload. `readme` points at `README.md`, `requires-python` tells pip to refuse installation on older Pythons, and `license` is MIT.
`[project.scripts]` creates the `mylang` command on the user's PATH. The value `mylang.__main__:main` means import `mylang/__main__.py` and call its `main()` function.
